name: Templo de Santo Domingo
desc: A baroque church so gold inside it feels illegal to see for free. Sunset on the plaza out front is the daily main event.

name: Monte Albán
desc: Zapotec pyramids on a flattened mountaintop with valley views forever. Five bucks to stand on top of 2,500 years.

name: Hierve el Agua
desc: A petrified waterfall with infinity pools carved by minerals, not influencers. Pack snacks, the view does the rest.

name: Árbol del Tule
desc: A 2,000-year-old tree so wide it makes buses look shy. One dollar to feel very small in the best way.

name: Jardín Etnobotánico
desc: Cacti arranged like sculpture behind old convent walls. The guided walk is the price of a fancy coffee and twice as calming.

name: Zócalo de Oaxaca
desc: Marimba bands, balloon sellers, and free people-watching under the laurels. The city's living room, open all night.

name: Mercado 20 de Noviembre
desc: The famous smoke hall where grilled meat clouds guide you like a beacon. Entry free, willpower not included.

name: Andador Calle Alcalá
desc: A cobbled pedestrian street of green stone buildings and gallery windows. Walk it slow, twice, for zero pesos.

name: Mitla
desc: Geometric stone mosaics older than your entire family tree. A quiet day trip that costs less than lunch.
